• Carbonation creates karst topography.
• Spheroidal weathering produces rounded rocks.
• Soil creep is the slowest mass movement.
• Vertical erosion dominates in youthful rivers.
• Sea level is ultimate base level.
Soil creep is the slowest mass movement.

items: Exams frequently ask to identify the slowest mass movement; the correct answer is always soil creep.
Note that vertical erosion (and v-shaped valleys) corresponds to youthful rivers.
Sea level is consistently tested as the ultimate base level for erosion.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Carbonation process leads directly to the formation of karst topography.
Spheroidal weathering causes concentric peeling that produces rounded rock structures.
Soil creep is uniquely identified as the slowest type of mass movement.
Youthful river systems are primarily dominated by vertical erosion rather than lateral erosion.
Sea level functions as the ultimate base level below which rivers cannot erode.
